---
title: "Introduction"
---

Tiny-DSA is a stylized debt-sustainability tool that projects a country's general-government debt-to-GDP ratio over a five-year horizon under a baseline macroeconomic and fiscal path and one configurable shock. It is intentionally minimal, implementing a single accounting identity recursed annually for five periods. The original Tiny‑DSA Excel workbook contained these calculations in fewer than sixty formula cells across three worksheets. The **tiny_dsa** Python package reimplements that logic programmatically, using a combination of programmatic extraction, machine translation, and AI.

> The **tiny_dsa** package is a methodological artifact prepared by Teal Insights. It is not intended for policy use, is not validated against country-specific data, and is not endorsed by the IMF, the World Bank, or any other institution. The modeling choices follow the standard public-debt accounting literature; the documentation conventions follow the IMF/World Bank LIC-DSF and IMF FAD Q-CRAFT guidance documents.

The intended reader is a domain economist familiar with the standard public-debt accounting identity. The tool projects in real terms throughout: the debt ratio and the primary balance are expressed as percentages of GDP, and real GDP growth and the real interest rate are expressed in percent per annum.

Tiny-DSA deliberately omits the contribution of inflation to the debt ratio, exchange-rate dynamics, currency decomposition of debt, residual financing terms (stock-flow adjustments, contingent liabilities), and any endogenous fiscal response. The fiscal stance is exogenous, the snowball factor is computed in real terms, and shocks are step changes to a single parameter from a configurable shock-year onward. These simplifications keep the model small enough to be hand-traceable end-to-end.

This User Guide explains how to set up scenarios, run projections, and interpret the outputs using the tiny_dsa Python package. The remainder of the guide is structured as follows. Section II provides a functional overview of the package’s API and core concepts. Section III walks through three illustrative scenarios for a fictional country, Borvelia. Section IV discusses the methodology in detail, including the debt-dynamics identity, shock specification, realism checks, and limitations.

**Installation**

Install the package from GitHub using [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
uv add git+https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-tiny-dsa
```

For correctness evidence, see [Excel parity validation](03-excel-parity-validation.qmd), which summarizes the exported-library differential test against the source workbook.
